content: This document is a supplement to the 2014 Consolidated Guidelines for HIV prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and care for key populations, published by the World Health Organization (WHO) in July 2015. It serves as a technical tool to assist countries in setting and monitoring targets for addressing HIV among key populations, including men who have sex with men, people in prisons and other closed settings, people who inject drugs, sex workers, and transgender individuals. The publication provides technical guidance for planning and evaluating the implementation of a comprehensive package of interventions aimed at addressing HIV in these populations. It is designed to help countries assess progress at the national and subnational levels, involving government agencies, non-governmental organizations (NGOs), communities, and service providers in the development, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of HIV programs. The framework builds on an existing WHO, UNODC, and UNAIDS technical guide for setting targets for universal access to HIV prevention, treatment, and care for people who inject drugs. It includes a set of harmonized indicators to evaluate the implementation of interventions, aligned with indicators used by other United Nations (UN) and donor agencies. These indicators are practical and meaningful, selected based on current practices and available evidence, and are intended to guide policy development and effective programming. The document emphasizes the importance of setting clear, ambitious, but achievable targets to scale up programs with the greatest possible impact. The target-setting process should involve multisectoral collaboration and meaningful participation of all key populations. Indicative targets are proposed for selected indicators to help countries calibrate their own targets and responses. The comprehensive package of interventions for key populations is divided into two parts: 1. Essential health sector interventions: Comprehensive condom and lubricant programming. Harm reduction interventions for substance use, including needle and syringe programs (NSP), opioid substitution therapy (OST), and naloxone. Behavioral interventions. HIV testing and counseling. HIV treatment and care. Prevention and management of co-infections and other comorbidities, including viral hepatitis, tuberculosis (TB), and mental health conditions. Sexual and reproductive health interventions, including contraception, diagnosis and treatment of sexually transmitted infections (STIs), and cervical screening. 2. Essential strategies for an enabling environment: Supportive legislation, policy, and financial commitment, including decriminalization of behaviors of key populations. Addressing stigma and discrimination, including in the health sector. Community empowerment. Addressing violence against people from key populations. The document also highlights the importance of using appropriate and inclusive language when referring to key populations, respecting their right to self-identify and ensuring that terminology evolves with time and context. This publication complements other WHO and UN documents that provide evidence-based recommendations for addressing HIV among key populations. These include guidelines on HIV prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and care, as well as specific recommendations for sex workers, men who have sex with men, transgender individuals, and people who inject drugs. It also references operational guidelines for monitoring and evaluating HIV programs for these populations. The content of this document is derived from existing WHO guidance and integrates programming for HIV, TB, hepatitis B and C, and STIs for key populations. It aims to support countries in developing effective national responses to HIV and related health challenges.
